newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Coconut Oil-Prices seen higher on USDA report.
newsitem.headline: Coconut Oil-Prices seen higher on USDA report.

text.p: Coconut oil prices are expected to rise this week on prospects of higher corn and soybean prices following news of lower than expected crop output in the United States, vegetable oil traders said on Monday.

"My fearless forecast is higher to steady due to report by the United States Department of Agriculture of lower than expected soybean and corn stock estimates and prospects of weak copra production in the first quarter this year," a trader said.

The USDA pegged 1996 U.S. corn output at 9.293 billion bushels, slightly below average trade expectations of 9.317 billion, and soybeans at 2.382 billion, also lower than traders estimate of 2.407 billion.

The USDA also lowered its estimate for 1996-1997 U.S. soybean carry over stocks next September 1 to 155 million bushels from the previous 180 million while the 1996-1997 U.S. corn carry over stocks forecast was trimmed to 959 million bushels from the previous 1.157 billion.
Soybean and corn oil are used as substitute for coconut oil.
A trader said he expected coconut oil prices to move higher within a range of $5 to $10 this week.
The trade group United Coconut Association of the Phils Inc said coconut oil for January/February shipment was last traded at $772.50 per tonne CIF.
Orders for February/March deliveries were last traded at an average $759.16 per tonne CIF while orders for March/April shipment were last traded at $761.50 per tonne CIF.
Traders also complained of tight copra supply despite bullish forecast by the state-agency Philippine Coconut Authority and UCAP of better harvests this year.
"Copra is so hard to find these days," said one local trader.
But another trader said he suspected some farmers and traders were holding on to some of their stocks for better prices.

Traders said two boats are scheduled to deliver coconut oil in Rotterdam in the next two weeks, one is arriving on January 20 and the other on January 28. "Their total shipments cannot be determined yet," a trader said.

Some 49,000 tonnes of coconut oil were exported to the United States and Rotterdam last month out of total export applications of 75,000 tonnes. "Deliveries of the 36,000 tonnes were delayed but are expected to be shipped this month," the trader said without giving additional details.
